02-real-two-day-roundtrip.alt: Line chart of QQQ, TQQQ, SQQQ and an idealized +3× series normalized to 100 on 17 April 2025, for 17, 21 and 22 April. QQQ dips to 97.52 and finishes at 100.09; TQQQ falls to 92.69 and finishes at 99.78; SQQQ rises to 107.38 and finishes at 99.07.
02-real-two-day-roundtrip.caption: A real two-session fall and recovery. QQQ fell and then rose back to just above its starting close, yet both the daily +3× product TQQQ and the daily −3× product SQQQ finished below their starting values.
02-real-two-day-roundtrip.assumptions: IBKR historical daily closing prices (regular trading hours), not adjusted for distributions; only ratios within the window are used. QQQ is a proxy for the Nasdaq-100. Selected by the documented rule in this notebook; one illustration, not evidence about frequency. Actual fund returns include fees, financing and tracking effects that three closes cannot separate.

03-matched-windows.alt: Two stacked charts over 20 trading days for three real QQQ windows that each rose about 8.5 to 9 percent with 12 positive days. Top: QQQ paths, one calm, one moderate and one very volatile with a drop of about 8 percent early on. Bottom: the idealized daily 3× product on the same days ends at about 126 for the window starting June 2022, about 128 for May 2023 and about 119 for April 2025, against a dashed line at about 126 for three times the QQQ gain.
03-matched-windows.caption: Three real 20-day QQQ windows with almost the same cumulative return (about +8.5% to +9%) and the same number of positive days (12 of 20). The idealized daily 3× product ends between about +19% and +28%, because the day-to-day path differs.
03-matched-windows.assumptions: IBKR historical daily closing prices, not adjusted for distributions. Windows found by the systematic rule in this notebook (largest 3× spread among non-overlapping windows with equal positive-day count and QQQ returns within 0.5 percentage points); selected to illustrate a mechanism, not randomly sampled. The 3× series is an idealized model of QQQ's own daily returns without fees, financing or tracking error.

03b-window-decomposition.alt: Grouped bar chart for the three 20-day QQQ windows. Each group shows a compounding benefit of about +2.2 to +2.5 percentage points, a volatility correction of −2.16 for June to July 2022, −1.00 for May 2023 and −8.24 for April to May 2025, and a net difference from naive 3× of +0.12, +1.47 and −6.03 percentage points.
03b-window-decomposition.caption: The three 20-day results split into a compounding benefit (solid), a volatility correction (striped) and their net, the compounding deviation from naive 3× (dark), in percentage points of the window's return. Below each window: naive 3× return → idealized 3× return. The compounding benefit is nearly the same in all three windows; the correction is not.
03b-window-decomposition.assumptions: Full-precision daily QQQ returns from IBKR closing prices (not adjusted for distributions); idealized 3× model without fees, financing or tracking error. Exact identity R3 = 3R + (3R²+R³) + (1+R)³(e^D − 1); the split is explanatory, not the unique decomposition of leveraged-ETF returns. Windows are those selected in section 3.

04-volatility-drag-rolling.alt: Scatter chart of 1,190 overlapping 63-day QQQ windows. Horizontal axis: realized volatility from about 11 to 39 percent. Vertical axis: the idealized 3× result relative to the cube of QQQ's growth, (1 + QQQ return)³, falling from about −1 percent at low volatility to about −10 percent at the highest volatility, closely following a dashed second-order model curve. Points are colored by QQQ's return over the window. A legend toggle shows the actual TQQQ results.
04-volatility-drag-rolling.caption: Across 1,190 overlapping 63-day QQQ windows, the idealized daily 3× result falls further below benchmark wealth cubed, (1 + QQQ return)³, as realized volatility rises, closely following the second-order approximation. Hover a point for its dates and returns; use the legend to add actual TQQQ.
04-volatility-drag-rolling.assumptions: IBKR historical daily closing prices (QQQ, TQQQ), 2021-10-11 to 2026-10-07, not adjusted for distributions. Overlapping windows are not independent (about 19 non-overlapping quarters). Gap = (1 + idealized 3× return) / (1 + QQQ return)³ − 1, where (1 + QQQ return)³ is benchmark wealth raised to the leverage power (a path-independent reference); to second order its logarithm is about −3 times the sum of squared daily returns. The dashed curve is exp(−3σ²T) − 1 with T = 63/252. Actual TQQQ includes fees, financing and tracking effects.

05-positive-days-rolling.alt: Box plots with every point shown, for 1,190 overlapping 63-day QQQ windows grouped by share of positive days, from 45 percent or fewer to more than 65 percent. Above each group is the share of its windows that ended above zero: 0.6, 32.2, 58.9, 92.6, 92.6 and 100.0 percent. The median idealized 3× return rises from about −33 percent to about +53 percent, but each group spans a wide range, for example from about −13 percent to +86 percent in the 55 to 60 percent group.
05-positive-days-rolling.caption: In this five-year sample, windows with a larger share of positive days were much more likely to finish with a positive idealized 3× return (percentages above each group), but the share of green days alone does not determine the result: windows in the same group end anywhere from a loss to a large gain, depending on the size of the daily moves.
05-positive-days-rolling.assumptions: IBKR historical daily closing prices of QQQ, 2021-10-11 to 2026-10-07, not adjusted for distributions; 63-day overlapping windows (about 19 independent quarters). The 3× series is an idealized model without fees, financing or tracking error.
